root_cause.text: In Btrfs `create_pending_snapshot()` the snapshot-creation path unconditionally treated `btrfs_uuid_tree_add()` failure for `BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL` as fatal, so repeated snapshots of a received subvolume could hit a UUID-tree leaf size overflow (`-EOVERFLOW`) and abort the transaction, forcing the filesystem read-only.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds special handling in `fs/btrfs/transaction.c` after `btrfs_uuid_tree_add(trans, new_root_item->received_uuid, BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL, objectid);` to ignore `-EOVERFLOW` (`if (ret == -EOVERFLOW) ret = 0;`) and the commit message says this overflow “turns the filesystem into RO mode” because “snapshotting a previously received snapshot a bunch of times” reaches a `BTRFS_UUID_KEY_RECEIVED_SUBVOL item overflow`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ignore UUID tree overflow during snapshot creation to prevent unnecessary transaction aborts on heavily snapshotted received subvolumes.
intent_record.what: The patch adds a check after `btrfs_uuid_tree_add()` in `create_pending_snapshot()`: if the returned error is `-EOVERFLOW`, it is converted to success by setting `ret = 0` before the existing error handling block. It also adds a comment explaining why this overflow condition should be ignored.
intent_record.how: When creating a snapshot for a received subvolume, hitting the UUID tree leaf-item limit no longer aborts the transaction. Snapshot creation can continue successfully even if the received-UUID entry cannot be added, while deletion and send/receive remain functional through existing fallback behavior.

grouping_result.intent: Ignore UUID tree overflow during snapshot creation to prevent unnecessary transaction aborts on heavily snapshotted received subvolumes.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it makes snapshot creation ignore UUID-tree overflow during received-subvolume snapshot handling, instead of treating the btrfs_uuid_tree_add() failure as fatal and aborting the transaction.

candidates.rationale: This conditional treats any UUID-tree insertion failure other than -EEXIST as fatal, which includes -EOVERFLOW from leaf size overflow during repeated received-subvolume snapshots, directly triggering transaction aborts.
This is the action that turns the UUID-tree overflow failure into a transaction abort, which is the harmful behavior described in the root cause.
This call can return -EOVERFLOW when the UUID tree leaf overflows on heavily snapshotted received subvolumes; the surrounding code mishandles that return value.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition treats every UUID-tree insertion failure except -EEXIST as fatal, so a benign -EOVERFLOW from repeated received-subvolume snapshots is not ignored and instead triggers the abort path.
This statement turns the handled UUID-tree insertion failure into a transaction abort, which is the harmful behavior that can force the filesystem read-only.
